narrative.overview: A portfolio drawn, not decorated — violet draughting ink laid over a warm engineering sheet. The canvas is a near-black ink carrying a two-layer measurement grid and a fine film grain, lit from the top-left like a drafting lamp. Type is a high-contrast serif for statements and a monospace for every coordinate; diagrams are framed, captioned figures, not screenshots in cards. The one live color is violet — it marks signal, never fills space. Motion is atmospheric (background bloom-drift + a recurring scanner sweep, plus a glowing footer dev-tree), never loud. The system's discipline is the argument: exact spacing, measured contrast, and a single restrained accent read as the same engineering rigor the work claims.
keyCharacteristics: Warm-ink canvas with an ever-present engineering grid + grain (never a flat solid).
Violet as signal only: accent strokes, active nav, primary CTA, one italic word.
Sharp corners everywhere; registration ticks instead of rounded cards.
Monospace coordinate labels carry all metadata.
Serif display statements over monospace scaffolding — contrast, not costume.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Violet is signal, not decoration. As primary accent it appears on ≤10% of any screen — strokes, active state, primary CTA, one emphasis word. The categorical domain hues are the one sanctioned exception, and only when color carries domain meaning.

rules.name: The Three-Domain Rule
rules.body: Jade / cobalt / violet mean Product·AI / Cloud / Security — and nothing else. Violet doubles as primary + Security; cobalt is Cloud only. Exactly three hues, each a fixed meaning, always paired with a text label. No fourth categorical hue; never repurpose one for decoration.

rules.name: The Warm-Ink Rule
rules.body: The neutral ramp is warm (bone → ink); the accent is cool (violet). Never warm the accent or cool the neutrals to match; the temperature split is the identity.

rules.name: The Coordinate Label Rule
rules.body: All metadata is monospace, uppercase, wide-tracked, prefixed with a marker (§00, a two-digit index). Metadata never uses the serif or body sans.

rules.name: The One Italic Rule
rules.body: Emphasis in a display statement is a single Fraunces italic word, optionally in violet. Never bold the serif; never italicize a whole line.

rules.name: The Flat-Sheet Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest and separated by 1px lines, never by shadow. The single exception is the violet Signal Bloom on primary-button hover.

dos: Do keep the engineering grid + grain present on every page background; never ship a flat solid ink fill.
Do hold violet to ≤10% of any screen — strokes, active state, primary CTA, one italic word.
Do set all metadata in monospace uppercase with a marker prefix.
Do keep body text at Bone Dim (#ddd9d2) or brighter; verify ≥4.5:1 on ink before shipping any new muted text.
Do frame diagrams as captioned figures recolored into the duotone, with registration ticks.
Do provide a prefers-reduced-motion fallback for every reveal and transition.
donts: Don't reintroduce the generic dark-neon dev site: slate-950 + cyan glow, glassmorphism panels, or radial gradient mesh.
Don't add flashy, animation-heavy spectacle. Motion stays atmospheric and subtle (bloom-drift, scanner sweep, footer dev-tree).
Don't round corners (except the 3px on inline code). No rounded cards, no pill radii.
Don't use neutral gray drop shadows; separate surfaces with 1px lines.
Don't warm the violet accent or cool the bone/ink neutrals to match.
Don't set metadata, eyebrows, or labels in the serif or body sans.
